items.author: hwchase17
items.how: You mention it in a Slack thread with a brief. Each thread gets its own sandbox (an isolated, disposable Linux machine with Chrome, FFmpeg...) where everything is made as code (a slide is HTML, a film is an animation timeline), so a change is an edit and a re-render. A router skill picks among 35 skills loaded only when needed, keeping the context window small. On big jobs the main agent splits the work and starts async subagents in parallel. Code checks colors, fonts, contrast and chart math before delivery. Two-layer memory (team and personal) keeps your rules, and after each job it writes notes on what worked. External tools (Notion, Linear, Figma) connect through MCP, each person signed…
items.title: Content Studio: LangChain's design agent, now open source
items.try: Apache 2.0 license, Python 3.11+, built on Deep Agents and deployable on Managed Deep Agents (LangSmith, paid); a local mode with no keys is advertised. GitHub stars not checked.
items.what: The agent LangChain uses internally as a designer: ask it in Slack for a visual, a slide or a launch video and it returns finished, on-brand files. Basically a junior designer available 24/7 in Slack.
items.who: A real case of an agent doing company work: per the README, over 3,000 assets shipped since August, and three in four requests come from outside marketing. A reusable architecture blueprint for any internal ops agent (Slack + sandbox + skills + memory + checks in code).

items.author: hwchase17
items.how: On each tool call the gateway (1) identifies the caller (a user, an agent or a shared profile); (2) blocks the call if a deny policy matches; (3) attaches the right stored credential instead of a token hardcoded in the agent; (4) asks a human to approve if an approval policy matches; (5) forwards the call to the MCP server and records a trace of who did what. Tool kits define which tools each agent sees, through a single URL.
items.title: LangSmith Tool Gateway: a bouncer for your agents' tools
items.try: Beta, LangSmith Plus and Enterprise plans only (paid), on LangSmith Cloud (GCP US/EU/APAC, AWS US).
items.what: A central layer between your agents and the tools they call, handling access, identity and rules. Like an IT department handing out badges instead of every agent holding the keys to the whole building.
items.who: As soon as several agents touch sensitive tools (CRM, email, finance), you need to know who sent what on whose behalf and to require approvals. Harrison Chase: the more goal-oriented agents get, the more crucial this fine-grained control becomes.

items.author: hwchase17
items.how: Per Izzy Miller (Hex), instead of hand-writing static context (docs, definitions) that goes stale, the system starts from that context and synthesizes knowledge organized as a graph of linked notions, enriched by real-world feedback, so it can be verified and maintained automatically. Site not reachable, limited details.
items.title: Hex Knowledge Engine: a self-maintaining company knowledge layer
items.what: A self-learning, graph-based context system built into Hex 4.0 (a data analysis tool), so data agents know the company's definitions and rules. Basically an internal wiki the AI keeps up to date on its own.
items.who: The real blocker for data agents is having five different definitions of revenue. Harrison Chase calls this a knowledge factory: at LangChain, a set of metric definitions and skills for fetching data from each system.

items.author: kieranklaassen
items.how: According to Replit, its Missions ran agent swarms (many agents in parallel) that explored thousands of workflows in the existing tool and rebuilt its features 1:1. No further details readable.
items.title: DataCat: an observability clone built by agent swarms
items.try: Announced as 100% free; license and status not checked. Site not reachable, limited details.
items.what: Replit announces DataCat, a free alternative to the leading observability platform (a tool that monitors an app and catches issues, billed at $83,700/yr according to Replit).
items.who: A striking demo of SaaS cloning by agents: if agents can copy an expensive tool, B2B software prices come under pressure. Treat it as a marketing claim until people test it.

items.author: zachlloydtweets
items.how: Announced path: fundamentals, then writing your first automation loop (an agent that keeps relaunching itself on tasks), up to a full factory with specs (written before the code), risk assessment and end-to-end verification (testing the whole flow, not one piece).
items.title: Warp Learn: a free course to build your software factory
items.try: Free and public, taught by @BHolmesDev. Site not reachable, limited details.
items.what: A hands-on course by Warp (the terminal) on building a software factory: per Zach Lloyd, an automation loop in the cloud that orchestrates agents to build better and better software over time.
items.who: For anyone moving from one-conversation-at-a-time vibe coding to agents that run continuously.
